details.detail: Surface detail: value, panel tone, seams, fastener rows, slat band, gear stripe, placards, grime
details.note: The near-far value is still reversed in w19A. The near flap is L163/161 at (600,440)/(560,500), and the far skin is L169/172 at (680,195)/(720,220); r12 had 173/174. The l.256 roughness ramp took only 3-4 L off. KN41 runs 194 near to 146 far. The new w12 flap streaks (l.334-339) read as three hard, evenly toned ruled bars per canoe in w26K (ratB13/z26K_flaps_r12_r13.png). They look like painted walkway lines, not the soft irregular grime in _7250. In the studio view c_canoes_left they render slightly lighter than the flap, because the streak material has no xSkin layer, no panel tint and no normal tilt. There is no tiling, and the seams and fastener rows are unchanged and correct.

The gap taper works. The near TE gap in w19A is now 2 px: row 400 x 562-563 (r12: 4 px, 561-564), row 470 3 px (r12: 5), row 520 3 px (r12: 6). That matches KN41's ~2 px at this width. The hierarchy is unchanged and correct.

The structure is restored on both sides. K side, w26K near pod at x=600: crown L201-223 (y 300-315), flank grading 177 -> 163 -> 148 (y 320-355), then a dark keel rim. In r12 the whole pod was a flat 189-191. A side, w19A: flank L132 at (470,350) and L124 at (515,240) against the near flap at 163, so 0.76-0.81 (r12: 0.61; KN41: 0.72-0.77), with a visible top-to-keel grade (ratB13/z19A_r12_r13.png). The sharper chine and the wedge tails read well in c_canoe_side. What remains: the K-side flank is still light. Against the 177-182 skin it is 0.94 at mid-flank and 0.82 low, where _7250 shows 0.54 on the near pod and 0.72 on the second pod (_7331: 0.41-0.51). The tip still ends on the u 0.998 ring (l.367) and shows a small faceted point in c_canoes_left (studio only).

The fairing is crisper, and the flank shade reads: w13A (520,290) and (560,300) went from L171 to L155. Geometry gap: in LALF _137 the fairing over the fan cowl is a defined hump that ends forward in a blunt, rounded nose with a seam at its base. The render still ramps down to a thin wedge that blends into the cowl, because w lerps from 0.05 and the ridge from 0 over x 1.4-3.2 (l.442-446). See ratB13/pylon_w13A_r12_r13_lalf137.png.

details.detail: Nacelle geometry (cowl, lip, splits, strake, access panel)
details.note: The cowl, lip, splits and strake are unchanged and correct. The access panel is still a sharp rounded rectangle. LALF _136 shows a stadium oval with a fastener ring and a fainter second panel below it (A w12 low, not fixed).

The sunlit K cowl no longer clips. In w11K, (380,350) went from L229 to 206, (420,400) from 226 to 201, and (460,480) from 212 to 173. Row 420 now rolls off 205 -> 192 across the face (r12: a flat 222-228). That is still a little hot and flat against knav _9, which peaks at 187 and runs 169 -> 97 down to the strake. The shade side in w13A and w11A is unchanged and correct. The s13A sun hotspot on the fan cowl is gone, and the monogram is unchanged and correct.

The bright floor is gone. c_nacelle_left (650,400) went from L157 to 25, w11K inner wall (335,450) from 172 to 35 and (345,500) from 179 to 27, and w11A from 61 to 8 at (595,420). It now overshoots into a void. LALF _136 (same seat as w11A) shows a dark slate liner at L31-87 with visible acoustic panel joints and an inner-lip band, while the render throat is L6-9. The blade ring still does not read in any view; only the spinner nub (L60) shows in c_nacelle_left. The read is now a black hole rather than a fan face (ratB13/inlet_c_vs_knav9.png).

With the camera at the glass, w26K shows the whole registration. It is in the same 180-degree-inverted reading as alv _7250 (ratB13/reg_26K_vs_7250.png), with the right stroke weight and spacing. The ink measures #27355c against KN41's navy #14538e/skin, and _7250 reads greyer (#57626f) under overcast. That is acceptable.
Unchanged. The red point sits at the tip in n19A and the discharger comb shows in w19A.

There is no z-fighting, floating part, gap or tiling. Residuals: the faceted canoe tip point (studio), the streak bars that read as ruled stripes, and stair-stepped aliasing on the long slat and spoiler hairlines in w26K (ratB13/reg_26K_vs_7250.png, top). The last is a lighting/AA matter.
